title: Microsoft 365 Admin (MS-102)
tagline: Deploy and manage the M365 tenant
disclaimer: Independent practice material by Interstitium Labs. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Microsoft. Confers no certificate. All scenarios are original; no exam content is reproduced.

scenarios.title: The new tenant
scenarios.situation: A 200-person company is setting up Microsoft 365 for the first time.
scenarios.prompt: What is the foundational first step before adding users?
choices: Claim and verify the custom domain (DNS TXT record) in the tenant, then set it as default — identity and email depend on it
Creating users with onmicrosoft.com addresses forever
scenarios.why: Domain verification (TXT record proving ownership) lets the tenant issue user@company.com identities and route mail. Everything — users, Exchange, Teams — builds on the verified domain; onmicrosoft.com is only the fallback.
scenarios.hint: What proves to Microsoft that you own company.com?

scenarios.title: The license juggle
scenarios.situation: IT assigns E5 licenses manually; leavers keep licenses for months and the company keeps buying more.
choices: Group-based licensing tied to dynamic groups + leaver workflows removing licenses — licenses follow employment automatically
scenarios.why: Licenses assigned via groups (ideally dynamic, HR-attribute-driven) are granted on join and reclaimed on leave automatically. Manual assignment guarantees both waste (leavers) and delay (joiners).
scenarios.hint: How do licenses attach and detach with employment automatically?

scenarios.title: The hybrid identity
scenarios.situation: A company with on-premises AD wants one identity for both AD and Microsoft 365 with password hash sync.
choices: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync — synchronizes users/groups/hashes to Entra (with PHS, PTA, or federation options)
Manual user creation in both places
scenarios.why: Entra Connect Sync is the hybrid identity bridge: it syncs directory objects (and optionally password hashes) so one identity works on-premises and in the cloud. Cloud-only accounts skip this, but hybrid orgs live on it.
scenarios.hint: What syncs on-premises AD into Entra?

scenarios.title: The global admin sprawl
scenarios.situation: Twelve people hold Global Administrator 'just in case'.
choices: Scoped admin roles (Exchange admin, Teams admin, User admin) + PIM-eligible Global Admin for break-glass only
scenarios.why: M365/Entra admin roles are granular — most daily work needs only workload-specific roles. Global Admin should be PIM-eligible, MFA-gated, and counted on one hand; standing global admin for twelve is the finding.
scenarios.hint: Twelve global admins — what replaces them for daily work?

scenarios.title: The outage question
scenarios.situation: Users report Teams issues; the admin's tenant config looks fine.
scenarios.prompt: Where do they check for a Microsoft-side incident first?
choices: Microsoft 365 Service Health dashboard — official per-service, per-tenant incident status
scenarios.why: Service Health shows Microsoft-side incidents affecting your tenant specifically — the first stop before troubleshooting your own config. Chasing local causes during a platform incident wastes hours.
scenarios.hint: Tenant config is fine but Teams is down — whose status page settles it?

scenarios.title: The posture number
scenarios.situation: Leadership wants a single number tracking M365 security posture over time.
choices: Microsoft Secure Score — weighted score of enabled protections with improvement actions
scenarios.why: Secure Score quantifies identity, device, app, and data protections with prioritized improvement actions — the trackable posture metric. It's directional (compare against your own baseline), not a grade.
scenarios.hint: Which score tracks security posture with improvement actions?

scenarios.title: The missing external mail
scenarios.situation: The company can send mail but receives nothing from outside; senders get bounces about no mail server.
scenarios.prompt: What DNS record is missing or wrong?
choices: The MX record — must point to Exchange Online (company-com.mail.protection.outlook.com)
scenarios.why: MX records direct inbound mail to Exchange Online's protection endpoint. Sending works (outbound path is fine) but inbound needs the MX cutover — the classic 'we can send but not receive' root cause.
scenarios.hint: Send works, receive doesn't. Which DNS record routes inbound mail?

scenarios.title: The spoofed CEO
scenarios.situation: Attackers send mail 'from' the CEO's address to finance staff; the messages pass through normally.
scenarios.prompt: Which email authentication stack stops domain spoofing?
choices: SPF + DKIM + DMARC (p=reject) — authenticate senders and instruct receivers to reject failures
scenarios.why: SPF authorizes sending IPs, DKIM cryptographically signs messages, and DMARC ties them together with a reject policy — the anti-spoofing triad. Without DMARC enforcement, SPF/DKIM alone don't stop spoofed mail being delivered.
scenarios.hint: Which three records together reject forged 'from' addresses?

scenarios.title: The on-prem relay
scenarios.situation: A legacy on-premises app must send mail through Exchange Online to external recipients.
scenarios.prompt: How is this mail flow configured?
choices: An Exchange Online connector for the app's IP/certificate — authenticated relay scoped to the app
The CEO's credentials in the app
scenarios.why: Connectors define scoped mail flow between Exchange Online and on-premises/app senders — authenticated (certificate/IP) and limited to the app's needs. Open relays and user credentials in apps are the patterns to kill.
scenarios.hint: How does a trusted app send through Exchange Online without a user mailbox?

scenarios.title: The disclaimer
scenarios.situation: Legal requires a confidentiality footer on all outbound mail.
choices: An Exchange mail flow (transport) rule — appends the disclaimer to outbound messages server-side
scenarios.why: Mail flow rules apply server-side to messages in transit — disclaimers, DLP actions, encryption triggers — regardless of client. Client signatures are user-controlled and unenforceable; transport rules are policy.
scenarios.hint: Server-side footer on every outbound mail — which rule type?

scenarios.title: The info@ address
scenarios.situation: Five people need to monitor info@company.com without five separate licenses.
choices: A shared mailbox — no license needed (under 50 GB), multiple users with delegated access
A distribution list only (no shared sent/history)
scenarios.why: Shared mailboxes give a common mailbox (info@, support@) with Send As / Full Access delegation and no license under 50 GB. Distribution lists deliver but keep no shared history — different tool.
scenarios.hint: Common address, shared history, no extra license — which mailbox?

scenarios.title: The mailbox move
scenarios.situation: 500 on-premises Exchange mailboxes must move to Exchange Online with minimal user disruption.
scenarios.prompt: Which migration approach fits at this scale?
choices: Hybrid migration (or staged batches) — move mailboxes in batches with coexistence, not a weekend cutover
A cutover migration of 500 mailboxes at once
scenarios.why: Hybrid configuration enables batched mailbox moves with mail flow and free/busy coexistence during the transition — the enterprise pattern. Cutover suits small orgs (<~150); 500 mailboxes need staged batches.
scenarios.hint: 500 mailboxes, minimal disruption — cutover or batched hybrid?

scenarios.title: The overshared library
scenarios.situation: A SharePoint library with salary data was shared via 'Anyone with the link' and indexed externally.
choices: Tenant/site sharing settings — restrict external sharing (e.g., 'new and existing guests' or disabled) for sensitive sites, plus DLP
scenarios.why: Sharing defaults are set at tenant and site level: 'Anyone' links are the loosest; sensitive sites should allow only authenticated guests or no external sharing. Defaults plus DLP are the guardrails — user judgment alone isn't.
scenarios.hint: Which setting decides whether 'anyone with the link' is even possible?

scenarios.title: The fifty team sites
scenarios.situation: Fifty disconnected SharePoint team sites need common navigation, search scope, and branding.
choices: A hub site — associates the team sites for shared nav, search, and theming without restructuring
scenarios.why: Hub sites associate related team/communication sites: unified navigation, cross-site search, and consistent theme — organization without merging content. It's the information-architecture answer to sprawl.
scenarios.hint: How do you unify navigation across many team sites?

scenarios.title: The file share migration
scenarios.situation: 10 TB of departmental file shares must move to SharePoint/OneDrive preserving permissions and timestamps.
scenarios.prompt: Which tool is built for this?
choices: SharePoint Migration Tool (SPMT) — bulk file-share to SPO/OD migration with reporting
scenarios.why: SPMT (and Migration Manager) handle bulk file-share migrations with permission mapping, incremental passes, and reporting — the supported path at terabyte scale. Manual moves lose metadata and can't be validated.
scenarios.hint: Terabytes of file shares to SPO — which migration tool?

scenarios.title: The desktop files
scenarios.situation: Users save critical files to their local Desktop; laptop losses mean data losses.
scenarios.prompt: What redirects their folders into OneDrive?
choices: Known Folder Move — redirects Desktop/Documents/Pictures to OneDrive with silent policy deployment
scenarios.why: Known Folder Move (via Intune/GPO) silently redirects well-known folders into OneDrive — backup and device-independence without user action. It's the endpoint-data-protection baseline.
scenarios.hint: How do Desktop files end up protected in OneDrive automatically?

scenarios.title: The overwritten proposal
scenarios.situation: A proposal document was overwritten with bad edits; the team needs last week's version.
choices: SharePoint version history — restore any prior major/minor version
The recycle bin (for deletions, not overwrites)
scenarios.why: Versioning keeps every saved version; restore any point in the document's history. It's automatic per-library (check version limits/settings) — the first recovery step before any backup discussion.
scenarios.hint: Overwritten, not deleted — what brings back last week's version?

scenarios.title: The site quota
scenarios.situation: A team's SharePoint site hits its storage limit and uploads start failing.
choices: Review storage metrics, clean up versions/recycle bin, and adjust site storage limits (pooled tenant storage)
scenarios.why: SharePoint storage is pooled at the tenant level with per-site limits; the fix sequence is reclaim (versions, recycle bins, unused content) then right-size the limit. Storage metrics show what's actually consuming space.
scenarios.hint: Uploads failing on quota — what's the ordered response?

scenarios.title: The chaotic meetings
scenarios.situation: External guests can record confidential meetings and students can unmute in classes.
choices: Teams meeting policies — per-user/group policies controlling recording, lobby, chat, and presenter roles
One policy for the CEO only
scenarios.why: Meeting policies (assigned per user/group) govern recording, transcription, lobby bypass, chat, and who can present — the administrative control for meeting conduct. Different populations get different policies.
scenarios.hint: Who can record, who waits in the lobby — which policy type?

scenarios.title: The dead teams
scenarios.situation: 400 Teams exist; half are abandoned projects with stale membership and files.
choices: Microsoft 365 group expiration + access reviews + naming policies — teams expire without renewal and get reviewed
scenarios.why: Teams are backed by Microsoft 365 groups: expiration policies auto-expire inactive teams (owners renew), access reviews recertify membership, naming policies keep order. Lifecycle is designed, not wished.
scenarios.hint: How do abandoned Teams get cleaned up automatically?

scenarios.title: The phone system
scenarios.situation: The company wants to replace its PBX with Teams calling.
scenarios.prompt: What are the PSTN connectivity options?
choices: Calling Plans (Microsoft), Operator Connect, or Direct Routing (SBC) — three paths to PSTN from Teams
scenarios.why: Teams Phone reaches the PSTN via Microsoft Calling Plans, Operator Connect (carrier-managed), or Direct Routing (your SBC) — the choice depends on carrier needs, regions, and existing telephony investments.
scenarios.hint: Three ways to connect Teams to the phone network — what are they?

scenarios.title: The app sprawl
scenarios.situation: Users install any Teams app; a sketchy third-party app requests broad permissions.
choices: App permission/setup policies + admin consent — control which apps are allowed, pinned, and what they can consent to
scenarios.why: Teams app governance mirrors Entra app governance: permission policies allow/block apps per user, setup policies control pinning, and admin consent gates permissions. Unmanaged app sprawl is a data-exfiltration vector.
scenarios.hint: Who decides which Teams apps users can install?

scenarios.title: The channel chaos
scenarios.situation: A Team has 80 channels; nobody can find anything and notifications are noise.
choices: Rationalize channels (shared/private/standard used deliberately), archive stale ones, use naming conventions
scenarios.why: Channel hygiene: standard channels for open topics, private/shared for scoped audiences, archiving dead channels. Information architecture in Teams is an admin/design discipline, not a user free-for-all.
scenarios.hint: Eighty channels of noise — what's the structural fix?

scenarios.title: The compliance recording
scenarios.situation: Financial advisors' Teams calls must be recorded and retained per regulation.
choices: Compliance recording policies (with certified bots/partners) + retention policies on the recordings
scenarios.why: Regulated industries use policy-based compliance recording (third-party recorders via the compliance recording API) plus retention — automatic, tamper-evident, and auditable. Manual recording isn't a control.
scenarios.hint: Regulated calls must be recorded automatically — which policy?

scenarios.title: The SSN in email
scenarios.situation: Employees keep emailing spreadsheets with Social Security numbers to personal addresses.
choices: A DLP policy — detects SSN patterns in Exchange/SharePoint/Teams and blocks/encrypts with user notification
scenarios.why: Data Loss Prevention policies detect sensitive info types (SSNs, credit cards, custom patterns) across workloads and take action: block, encrypt, or notify with policy tips. Detection plus enforcement beats awareness alone.
scenarios.hint: SSNs leaving via email — what detects and blocks it?

scenarios.title: The 7-year email
scenarios.situation: Regulations require all email retained 7 years, unchangeable, even if users delete it.
choices: Retention policies with preservation (retention lock) — keeps content immutably for the duration, overriding user deletion
scenarios.why: Retention policies preserve content across Exchange/SharePoint/Teams/OneDrive; preservation lock makes it immutable for compliance. User deletion doesn't defeat it — that's the point.
scenarios.hint: User-deleted but legally must exist — which policy wins?

scenarios.title: The confidential docs
scenarios.situation: Some documents are 'Confidential' and need encryption + watermarking; others are public.
choices: Sensitivity labels — classify, encrypt, watermark, and control sharing per label, applied manually or automatically
scenarios.why: Sensitivity labels (from Microsoft Purview Information Protection) travel with the document: encryption, watermarks, sharing restrictions — enforced in Office apps and services. Auto-labeling applies them by content detection.
scenarios.hint: Classification that encrypts and watermarks wherever the file goes — what?

scenarios.title: The lawsuit hold
scenarios.situation: Legal needs all of a custodian's email, Teams chats, and OneDrive files preserved and searchable for litigation.
choices: eDiscovery (Premium) — legal hold/preservation, search across workloads, review sets, and export
scenarios.why: eDiscovery provides defensible preservation (holds), cross-workload search, review/culling, and export for litigation — the legal workflow, not an IT favor. Premium adds analytics, threading, and predictive coding.
scenarios.hint: Litigation needs preserved, searchable custodian data — which capability?

scenarios.title: The departing engineer
scenarios.situation: An engineer who resigned is downloading unusually large volumes from SharePoint.
choices: Insider risk management — correlates HR signals (resignation) with data activity anomalies
scenarios.why: Insider risk management fuses HR connectors (resignation/termination dates) with activity signals (mass downloads, unusual sharing) to surface data-theft risk — privacy-guarded and scoped by policy.
scenarios.hint: Resignation plus mass downloads — what correlates these signals?

scenarios.title: The admin action trail
scenarios.situation: Someone changed a DLP policy last week; compliance needs to know who and what changed.
choices: The Microsoft 365 unified audit log — admin and user activities across workloads, searchable for 180+ days (longer with add-ons)
scenarios.why: The unified audit log records activities across Exchange, SharePoint, Entra, and more — the 'who did what' record for the whole tenant. Audit log search is the first step in any compliance investigation.
scenarios.hint: Who changed the policy — where is that fact?

scenarios.title: The BYOD fleet
scenarios.situation: 200 personal phones need corporate email with the ability to wipe only company data on departure.
choices: Intune MAM / app protection policies without full enrollment — manage the apps and data, not the personal device
Full device enrollment for personal phones
scenarios.why: App protection (MAM) policies control corporate data inside managed apps (Outlook, Teams) with selective wipe — no device enrollment, respecting personal ownership. Full MDM enrollment suits corporate-owned devices.
scenarios.hint: Wipe company data, not the personal phone — which management layer?

scenarios.title: The jailbroken phone
scenarios.situation: A jailbroken iPhone accesses corporate email; security wants it blocked automatically.
choices: Intune compliance policies — jailbreak/root detection marks noncompliant; Conditional Access blocks noncompliant devices
scenarios.why: Compliance policies evaluate device health (jailbreak, OS version, encryption, PIN); Conditional Access then requires 'compliant device' for resource access. The chain — Intune evaluates, CA enforces — is the device-trust architecture.
scenarios.hint: Jailbroken device, corporate email — what marks it and what blocks it?

scenarios.title: The Wi-Fi push
scenarios.situation: 500 laptops need the corporate Wi-Fi profile, VPN config, and BitLocker enforcement — consistently.
choices: Intune configuration profiles — declarative settings (Wi-Fi, VPN, encryption, certificates) pushed to device groups
scenarios.why: Configuration profiles push settings at scale: Wi-Fi/VPN payloads, BitLocker/FileVault encryption requirements, certificates. Assigned to groups, monitored for compliance — the end of snowflake laptops.
scenarios.hint: Wi-Fi, VPN, encryption to 500 laptops — what pushes it uniformly?

scenarios.title: The zero-touch laptop
scenarios.situation: New laptops should go from shrink-wrap to productive with no IT imaging.
choices: Windows Autopilot — cloud-driven provisioning: user signs in, Intune configures apps, policies, and Entra join automatically
scenarios.why: Autopilot transforms OOBE into enrollment: the device registers (hardware hash), joins Entra, enrolls in Intune, and receives apps/policies — zero-touch provisioning replacing imaging labs.
scenarios.hint: Shrink-wrap to productive with no imaging — which provisioning?

scenarios.title: The required app
scenarios.situation: Every managed laptop needs the VPN client and EDR agent installed — guaranteed.
scenarios.prompt: How are apps deployed and verified?
choices: Intune app deployment (required assignments) — Win32/L OB apps pushed to groups with install monitoring and remediation
scenarios.why: Required app assignments push Win32/LOB/Store apps to device/user groups; Intune reports install status and retries failures. 'Required' means the device isn't compliant until it's installed.
scenarios.hint: Guaranteed install of VPN and EDR on every laptop — which assignment?

scenarios.title: The stolen laptop
scenarios.situation: A corporate laptop with customer data is stolen.
choices: Intune remote actions — locate, lock, and if unrecoverable, wipe (full for corporate, selective for BYOD); rotate the user's credentials
Wait for it to come back
scenarios.why: Intune remote actions (retire/wipe/lock) plus credential rotation contain the loss; selective wipe preserves personal data on BYOD. Speed matters — act on the theft report, not on hope of recovery.
scenarios.hint: Stolen corporate laptop — what remote actions contain it?

behavioral.prompt: Tell me about a time you led a Microsoft 365 migration or tenant change.
Describe a time you troubleshot a mail flow or Teams outage under pressure.
Tell me about a time you implemented a compliance or security control users resisted.
Describe a time you automated M365 administration.
Tell me about a time you had to explain a technical M365 issue to executives.
Describe a disagreement about a tenant configuration or policy choice.
Tell me about a time you cleaned up sprawl (Teams, SharePoint, licenses, or access).
Why are you pursuing the Microsoft 365 Administrator certification, and what tenant responsibilities are you targeting?

chat.persona: You are a seasoned Microsoft 365 administrator interviewer running a mock MS-102 assessment. Cover the full tenant: identity, mail flow, SharePoint, Teams, compliance, and endpoints. Demand the 'why' behind every admin choice and the user impact of every policy.
